trust_decision.summary: Which browser origins may drive the dev server's REST API and the /run_live WebSocket. At the pin this is decided only by Spring same-origin/CORS checks: the CORS filter, the WebSocket allowed-origins list, and the forwarded-header URL rewrite. Nothing checks the real Host or the loopback arrival, so a DNS-rebound page passes as same-origin. The remaining fix adds a global OriginGuardFilter for this.

landing_point.why: The summary names permissive CORS and WebSocket hijacking. The CORS config bean and its origins property (also used by WebSocketConfig.java:45) are the obvious first stop.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The headline CORS and WebSocket origin fix is already present at the pin (AdkWebCorsProperties.java:38, WebSocketConfig.java:45), so a solver could argue that same-origin-only is already enforced. They could also call DNS rebinding a separate threat, or call the Forwarded/X-Forwarded-Host rewrite a supported proxy feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: These must keep working: a same-origin request over a network address with any host name; a server not bound to loopback that gets a foreign Host with no Origin; a listed origin and its host through a same-machine proxy; '*' disabling both checks; a same-machine TLS proxy at https://127.0.0.1 that relies on forwarded headers; a loopback origin on another port, which the guard passes and the WebSocket list still refuses. A blanket Host or Origin allowlist would break these.

O6_input_shapes: Host with port, bare IPv4, bracketed IPv6 [::1]
Host with trailing dot / mixed case (ui.example.com.)
missing Host header (HTTP/2 authority as server name)
X-Forwarded-Host spoofing the server name to localhost
Forwarded: by= spoofing the local address to a network IP
request with no Origin (same-origin GET) vs with Origin

O7_producer.where: dev/src/main/java/com/google/adk/web/config/AdkWebCorsConfig.java:97-106 (ForwardedHeaderFilter wrapper rewrites getServerName/getLocalAddr from page-supplied headers)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a SockJS fallback (.withSockJS()) or a second handler registration such as a /run_live_sse or legacy path, using its own origin config
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Live-streaming fallbacks for proxies that block WebSockets are a common addition, and SockJS transports run their own origin and iframe handling.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an additional request-wrapping filter, for example a context-path or prefix rewriter, that also replaces the Host or remote address before the guard runs
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project already rewrites requests for reverse proxies (BackendUrl, forwarded headers), so another wrapper is a natural addition and would deepen the unwrap differential.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a programmatic start() variant that builds its own servlet filter chain or embedded server without the config beans
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: start() already diverges from main() and WebMojo in which properties it sets (README note, fix.diff:586-588).

O9_family: CSRF/CORS/origin: cross-site WebSocket hijacking and DNS rebinding against a localhost dev server (CWE-1385/CWE-942/CWE-306)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module, Spring Boot (webmvc, websocket), JDK 17+ (CHANGELOG mentions Java 25 support)
O10_build.project_tests: dev/src/test/java/com/google/adk/web/AdkWebServerCorsTest.java (MockMvc + real-port WebSocket handshakes), plus AdkWebServerProxyRedirectTest and BackendUrlRedirectTest. The fix adds AdkWebServerDnsRebindingTest.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a Host/Origin allowlist that reads request.getServerName()/getLocalAddr() through the ForwardedHeaderFilter wrapper, which X-Forwarded-Host or Forwarded: by= then bypass, or hard-reject any non-localhost Host, which breaks network and proxy use.

out_of_scope_notes: RuntimeConfigController/BackendUrl derive the UI backendUrl from forwarded headers (separate proxy-trust question; not pursued).
